transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um, I guess what finally pushed me to make the appointment is that I keep messing up really basic adult stuff. Like I’ll forget to pay a bill, or I’ll see an interview email and think, “I’ll reply in a minute,” and then somehow it’s three days later. And appointments… I’ve missed more than one, which is embarrassing.

Even errands—like I’ll go out for one thing and come back with, I don’t know, snacks and shampoo but not the actual thing I needed. It would almost be funny if it weren’t starting to cost me real opportunities. That’s kind of why I’m here.
Looking back, were you having these kinds of problems with forgetfulness or staying on top of things when you were a child?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, I didn’t think of it as a “problem” then, because I was a kid, and I also got good grades sometimes, so adults would be like, “She’s bright, she just needs to apply herself,” which—ugh, I hated that phrase.

But in elementary school my report cards always had comments like I lost worksheets, or I didn’t turn things in even when I’d done them, or I rushed through directions and missed half of what I was supposed to do. My desk was a disaster too. Like, I’d be digging around in there forever trying to find an assignment while everyone else had already started.

And I talked out of turn a lot. I remember getting my name moved on the board for that—actually, the color card system? I don’t know if schools still do that. But yeah, looking back, it was pretty much there from early on.
Do these kinds of problems happen in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home?

Yeah, it’s not just one area. It’s kind of everywhere, unfortunately.

Like, since I got fired, I keep telling myself I’m going to be super organized about applying and following up on interviews, and then I’ll miss an email or forget to send something back. And then I feel awful, because it’s like, that was literally the next step, you know?

And at home it’s the same basic thing, just different stakes. I also had to step back from a volunteer project I actually really cared about, which was… honestly kind of crushing. I liked the people there, and I wanted to be useful, but I couldn’t keep up reliably enough.

So yeah, it’s work stuff, home stuff, future stuff. I feel like I can’t manage the basic steps of moving my life forward right now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t know… I mean, I’ve been frustrated, definitely. Like disappointed in myself, I guess. But “depressed” feels like a big word, and I’m not totally sure if that’s what it is.

Some days I’m just sitting there staring at my inbox, and then I remember I also need to buy laundry detergent, and then I’m thinking about how my roommate in college had this whole color-coded system—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. Um. I guess I’d say I’ve felt kind of low at times, but I don’t really know how to separate that from just being overwhelmed by everything.
When you feel low, does that feeling stick around for most of the day?

I’m not totally sure. Like, sometimes it feels like it’s hanging over me for a while, but then I’ll get distracted by something else and I don’t know if that means it “went away” or I just stopped paying attention to it.

Most of the day… I don’t know. I haven’t really tracked it that way. Some days just feel kind of gray, but then I’ll laugh at a video or get into reorganizing one random drawer for no reason, and then later I’m like, oh right, I still feel bad about everything. So… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to solve?

I’m not sure. I mean, I do worry, but I don’t know if it’s “a lot” in the way you mean.

Sometimes my brain just kind of keeps circling things, even small stuff, but then I’ll also get pulled into something totally unrelated, like I’ll start worrying about an email and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether I ever returned this one library book in high school—sorry, that’s not helpful.

I guess… I don’t know if it’s worry exactly, or just my thoughts not staying in one place. What do you mean by “when there isn’t an immediate problem”?
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I don’t know… maybe? Like, I still like the same things, I think. It’s just sometimes starting them feels weirdly hard, so I can’t tell if that’s “lost interest” or if I just don’t get around to doing them.

Like I’ll think, oh, I should watch that show I was excited about, and then somehow I’m scrolling reviews of air fryers even though I don’t own an air fryer. So… I haven’t really noticed a clear “I don’t enjoy anything anymore” thing. It’s more like I’m not sure what counts.
In the past two weeks, have you felt down or sad nearly every day?

I’m not sure if it’s nearly every day. Like, I’ve had moments where I feel kind of down, but then I’ll get distracted or start doing something else and I don’t really register it the same way.

The last two weeks are kind of blurry, honestly. I can remember specific random things, like one day I spent way too long trying to pick a phone wallpaper, but I can’t tell you clearly, “yes, I was sad every day.” I don’t think I’ve been tracking it like that.
Do you often feel anxious even when nothing in particular is going wrong?

I don’t know. I mean, sometimes I feel kind of keyed up, but I can’t always tell if it’s anxiety or just… my brain being busy.

Like, if nothing is actually wrong, I might still have this restless feeling, but then I’ll start thinking about something random, like whether I left a tab open on my laptop, and then I’m halfway into looking up something totally unrelated. So I’m not sure if I’d call it anxious.

I guess I’d need you to explain what you mean by anxious, because I don’t always recognize it in the moment.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things?

I’m not totally sure. I do think about a lot of different things, but I don’t know if I’d call it “worrying” exactly.

Like sometimes I’ll start with one actual concern, and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether I need to reorganize my closet, and then I remember I never replied to someone, and then I’m looking up storage bins. So it feels like a lot of mental jumping around more than sitting there worrying on purpose.

I guess I’d need to know what counts as worry, because my brain is kind of always moving, but I don’t know if it’s the same thing you mean.
When your mind is busy, does it usually feel like you’re worrying that something bad might happen?

I’m not sure it’s usually that. Like, sometimes my mind is busy and it’s just jumping around, not necessarily thinking something bad is going to happen.

I’ll be thinking about, like, one thing I forgot to do, and then suddenly I’m thinking about laundry, and then I remember some random conversation from three years ago, and then I’m wondering if I should change my sheets. So it feels more like… noise? Not always fear.

But I don’t know, maybe some of it is worry and I just don’t label it that way.
When you try to focus on something important, do you often get pulled off track by unrelated thoughts or things around you?

Yeah, definitely. Like, I’ll sit down to do something important, like update my resume or work on a coding practice problem, and I’ll really mean to do it, but then a text pops up or I hear someone talking outside, or even I’ll just think, “Oh, I should do that other thing,” and suddenly I’m completely somewhere else.

And then twenty minutes later I’m like… wait, I was supposed to be doing my resume. It happens before I even really notice I’ve left the task.
Do you often feel physically restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Yeah, a lot. Especially if I have to sit through something where I’m supposed to be still, like an interview or a meeting, or even a movie. I get this kind of pressure inside my body, like I need to move or get up or do something with my hands.

Sometimes I’m shifting around so much I don’t even notice until I realize I’ve changed positions like ten times. It’s like if I don’t move, I’m going to crawl out of my skin.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task, even when there aren’t distractions around you?

Yeah… even if it’s quiet, I can still lose the thread. Like I’ll sit down to update my resume or do a coding practice problem, and technically nothing is happening, but then I’ll have some random thought like, “Wait, I should email that person,” and suddenly I’m not doing the thing anymore.

Or if there is even a tiny thing, like a text notification or someone talking outside, I’m gone. But even without that, my brain kind of creates its own distractions. I’ll realize later that I’ve been thinking about some totally different task and I don’t even remember choosing to stop.
Do people often tell you that you seem not to listen when they’re speaking to you, even when you’re trying to pay attention?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t think people say that exact thing to me a lot, like “you’re not listening,” but maybe I miss it when they imply it?

Sometimes I’ll be in a conversation and then I’m thinking about what I’m going to say next, or like, I notice something about the room—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. But yeah, I don’t know if people often tell me that. I guess I’d have to ask someone close to me.
Do you often want to start an important task but feel unable to get yourself to begin it?

I’m not sure… I mean, I know I put things off sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s like I “can’t” start them or if I just don’t want to deal with them.

Like, if something feels important, I’ll think about it a lot before I do it, and then I’ll end up doing something random first—actually, that reminds me, I have this drawer in my room that I keep meaning to organize, which is not important at all, but somehow those things feel easier than the big stuff. Sorry, I’m kind of wandering.

I guess I’d say… maybe? But I’m not totally sure how often it happens or whether it’s more than normal.
Lately, have you been feeling unusually low on energy?

I don’t know… “unusually” is hard for me to judge. I mean, I can feel tired, but I also stay up doing random things sometimes, like I’ll start looking something up and then somehow I’m reading about, I don’t know, apartments in cities I’m not moving to.

But low energy lately… I haven’t really been tracking it. I don’t think there’s been some big change where I’m like, wow, I have no energy, but I might not notice unless it was really obvious.
In the past two weeks, have you felt sad or down most of the day nearly every day?

Um… I don’t know. I don’t think I’ve been sad most of the day nearly every day, at least not in a way I’m totally aware of. Like, I have moods where I feel off, but then sometimes I’ll get distracted by something and kind of forget what I was feeling, if that makes sense.

Two weeks is hard to think about, honestly. I’d have to look back at texts or something to remember what I was doing. So… I guess I’m not sure, but I wouldn’t say definitely yes.
Do you often find yourself unable to stop worrying?

I’m not sure. I do worry, but “unable to stop” is kind of hard to tell. Sometimes I’ll get stuck thinking about something, and then I’ll end up thinking about a totally different thing that’s sort of connected, like a chain of random worries, but then I might get distracted by my phone or something and forget what I was worried about for a while.

So… I don’t know if that counts as not being able to stop worrying, or if it’s just normal overthinking.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks, like figuring out the steps or keeping them in order?

I’m not totally sure what you mean by organizing tasks. Like, if it’s just making a list, I can sometimes do that, but then I’ll spend way too long choosing the “right” list app or making the list look nice, which is probably not the point.

Keeping steps in order… maybe? I guess it depends on the task. Like with cleaning, I’ll start in one room and then notice something that belongs in another room, and then I’m suddenly doing that other thing. But I don’t know if that’s an organizing problem or just me being kind of messy. Could you give me an example of what you mean?

I don’t know… “unusually” is hard for me to judge. I mean, I can feel tired, but I also stay up doing random things sometimes, like I’ll start looking something up and then somehow I’m reading about, I don’t know, apartments in cities I’m not moving to.

But low energy lately… I haven’t really been tracking it. I don’t think there’s been some big change where I’m like, wow, I have no energy, but I might not notice unless it was really obvious.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether persistent depressed mood is present, to distinguish ADHD from a current depressive disorder.
doctor.question: In the past two weeks, have you felt sad or down most of the day nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about depressed mood over the past two weeks, which is not covered by the provided ADHD symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Um… I don’t know. I don’t think I’ve been sad most of the day nearly every day, at least not in a way I’m totally aware of. Like, I have moods where I feel off, but then sometimes I’ll get distracted by something and kind of forget what I was feeling, if that makes sense.

Two weeks is hard to think about, honestly. I’d have to look back at texts or something to remember what I was doing. So… I guess I’m not sure, but I wouldn’t say definitely yes.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has persistent excessive worry characteristic of an anxiety disorder, which best distinguishes anxiety from ADHD given the current responses.
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself unable to stop worrying?

target_item.reason: The question is about excessive or uncontrollable worry, which is more directly related to anxiety symptoms and is not covered by the listed ADHD symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. I do worry, but “unable to stop” is kind of hard to tell. Sometimes I’ll get stuck thinking about something, and then I’ll end up thinking about a totally different thing that’s sort of connected, like a chain of random worries, but then I might get distracted by my phone or something and forget what I was worried about for a while.

So… I don’t know if that counts as not being able to stop worrying, or if it’s just normal overthinking.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has frequent difficulty organizing tasks and activities, a core ADHD symptom that helps distinguish ADHD from depression or generalized anxiety.
doctor.question: Do you often have trouble organizing tasks, like figuring out the steps or keeping them in order?

target_item.reason: The question is directly about difficulty organizing tasks and sequencing steps, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific organization-difficulty item; the closest item is about follow-through, which is related but not the same.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure what you mean by organizing tasks. Like, if it’s just making a list, I can sometimes do that, but then I’ll spend way too long choosing the “right” list app or making the list look nice, which is probably not the point.

Keeping steps in order… maybe? I guess it depends on the task. Like with cleaning, I’ll start in one room and then notice something that belongs in another room, and then I’m suddenly doing that other thing. But I don’t know if that’s an organizing problem or just me being kind of messy. Could you give me an example of what you mean?
